terms.definition: A configured LLM service endpoint the gateway can route queries to. May be local (running on the same machine) or cloud (remote API).
The registry of all configured backends and their current availability state maintained at runtime.
A single request from a developer submitted to the gateway for routing and processing by a backend.
The output of the routing step: which backend was selected for a given query and the reason for selection.
The component that analyses a query and assigns it a complexity tier to inform routing.
The component that selects a backend for a query based on its complexity tier, configured priority, and backend availability.
A categorical label assigned to a query by the Classifier indicating how capable a backend needs to be to handle it. Examples: simple, moderate, complex.
The automatic selection of the next available backend when the preferred backend is unavailable or returns an error.
A persisted record of a single processed query including the backend used, routing decision, response latency, and outcome.
The latency added by the gateway's classification and routing logic on top of the backend's own response time.
A backend running as a process on the same machine as the gateway, accessed via localhost.
A backend accessed via a remote HTTP API, typically requiring an API key for authentication.
Conforming to the request and response format of the OpenAI Chat Completions API, allowing clients built for OpenAI to work without modification.
The user-configured ranked list of backends the Router consults in sequence when selecting a backend for a query.
An explicit instruction from the developer to route a query to a specific backend, bypassing classification and priority logic.
